chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan from Abdullah ibn Sinan said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Ali (peace be upon him), when a client (mawla) of his died and left behind relatives, he did not take anything from his inheritance.
And he would say, "And those of kinship among each other have greater share [in inheritance] among themselves in the Book of Allah."'

key_terms.مَوْلًى: Client or freed slave under the patronage of another

ai.seo_question: Does the Imam inherit from his mawla if the mawla has living relatives?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) cites the Quranic principle of 'Awl al-Qarabah' (priority of kinship) to demonstrate that the Mawali relationship does not supersede blood ties in inheritance. This ruling, attributed to Imam Ali (AS), highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that the master's right to inherit is subordinate to that of the deceased's biological relatives, reinforcing the sanctity of familial bonds over clientage.
